name: 17080-chunkedprefill-8b-pp2
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3 -- two GPUs of one a3 node (--gres=gpu:2), one node.
parallelism: PP=2, TP=1, DP=1, V1 engine core under the Ray distributed executor; at this version V1 accepts pipeline parallelism only under Ray, so the executor is part of the topology.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM dense decoder: 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, hidden 4096, bf16, 8.03B params; the 32 layers split evenly 16/16 across the two pipeline stages.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), 2 streams, 150 requests, 520 s safety cap; warmup drops the first 15 by completion and the declared cooldown resolves past the end of the run, so 135 requests are scored. Closed loop rather than open loop deliberately: the engine is constructed INSIDE the guidellm process and takes 165-220 s to come up, while an open-loop arrival clock starts before it does -- so every arrival whose scheduled time falls inside construction is delivered as one burst the instant the engine is ready, and how big that burst is depends on how long startup happened to take. A closed-loop profile has no arrival clock: exactly `streams` requests are in flight from whenever the engine is ready, so the delivered load cannot vary with startup. The run-level `duration`, `requests_per_second` and `request_concurrency` fields come back pinned near the safety cap and should not be quoted; the declared metrics are per-request and unaffected.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, 8000 prompt tokens and 280 output tokens, both fixed (min = max = mean), no prefix buckets; `backend.request_format: plain` in scenario.json passes the prompt through untemplated so the engine sees exactly 8000 tokens, and the backend sets ignore_eos so every generation runs its full 280.
purpose: A long-document summarizer on an 8-billion-parameter model, serving two concurrent 8,000-token requests across two GPUs.
launch:
model: unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

pipeline-parallel-size: 2
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# LOAD-BEARING: at this engine version the V1 core accepts pipeline parallelism only under the
# Ray executor and refuses it under `mp`, falling back to V0.
distributed-executor-backend: ray

enable-chunked-prefill: true
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048
max-model-len: 16384
enable-prefix-caching: false
disable-log-requests: true
dtype: bfloat16
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
